subject: Biotechnology
title: What Is Pharmacogenomics
description: A micro-lesson that makes What Is Pharmacogenomics usable.

hook.text: The same dose of the same drug helps one patient and poisons another — their genes explain why.

buildup.text: Pharmacogenomics studies how genetic variants affect drug metabolism, efficacy, and side effects.

discovery.text: CYP2D6 metabolizes 25% of all drugs — poor metabolizers accumulate toxic levels, ultra-rapid ones get no benefit.

twist.text: Ethnic differences in CYP2D6 are dramatic — 30% of East Africans are ultra-rapid metabolizers versus 2% of East Asians.

climax.text: The FDA lists over 300 drugs with pharmacogenomic information on their labels — genotype before you prescribe.

punchline.text: Right drug, right dose, right patient — pharmacogenomics personalizes prescriptions.

quiz.question: What is the clinical significance of CYP2D6 genetic variants?
options: CYP2D6 determines a patient's blood type
Variants affect how quickly patients metabolize 25% of all drugs, causing toxicity or treatment failure
CYP2D6 controls the immune response to all medications

details.summary: Pharmacogenomics studies how genetic variation affects individual responses to drugs, explaining why the same medication works well for some patients but causes severe side effects or fails entirely in others.
details.whyItMatters: Adverse drug reactions cause over 100,000 deaths annually in the US alone. Many are predictable from genetic testing. Pharmacogenomics can prevent these reactions and identify the most effective treatment from the start, saving lives and reducing
takeaways: Genetic variants alter drug metabolism, efficacy, and side effect risk
Over 300 FDA drug labels include pharmacogenomic information
Testing before prescribing can prevent adverse reactions and treatment failures

faq.question: Why do people respond differently to the same drug?
faq.answer: Genetic variants in drug-metabolizing enzymes alter how fast drugs are activated or cleared. Variants in drug targets change sensitivity. Immune system genes determine hypersensitivity risk.

faq.question: How many drugs have pharmacogenomic guidelines?
faq.answer: CPIC has published guidelines for over 45 drug-gene pairs. The FDA lists pharmacogenomic information on over 300 drug labels. Common examples include clopidogrel-CYP2C19, warfarin-VKORC1, codeine-CYP2D6, and abacavir-HLA-B*57:01. The list grows as clinical evidence accumulates.
